explain.say: Imagine a band where everyone plays the drums. Loud, yes, but not much of a song! Now add a guitar, a flute and a singer. Look at the board. It asks why a mix of different people makes a group stronger. Diversity means having lots of different kinds of people together.

explain.say: See the first reason, more ideas? People who grew up in different places, with different families and abilities, think of different answers. When a group must solve a problem, more ideas means more chances to find a good one. Has a friend ever thought of something you never would?

faq.a: Diversity means having many different kinds of people together: different cultures, languages, religions, abilities, ages, genders and ideas.

faq.q: How does diversity give more ideas?
faq.a: People with different backgrounds and experiences notice different things and suggest different solutions, so a mixed group has more ideas to choose from.
asks: Why do different people think differently?

faq.q: How do different people help spot mistakes?
faq.a: When everyone thinks alike, they share the same blind spots. A person with a different view or experience can notice a problem the others missed.

faq.q: What can I learn from people who are different from me?
faq.a: New languages, foods, games, stories, skills and ways of seeing the world. It also helps you understand and respect others.
asks: Why make friends with different people?

faq.a: Inclusion means making sure everyone in a group is welcomed, respected and listened to, so they can take part fully. Diversity is who is in the room; inclusion is everyone being heard.

facts: In a 2008 study, groups with a newcomer from outside the friend group solved a murder-mystery puzzle more accurately, though members felt less comfortable (Phillips and others).
Many countries are very diverse: Indonesia has hundreds of ethnic groups and more than 700 languages.
